questions.q: Per this lesson, what is a regulator actually checking when auditing an organization's data governance?
options: Whether the organization can demonstrate control over the small number of elements that feed regulatory filings and financial statements
Whether every single column in every database is perfectly documented
Whether the organization uses a specific database vendor
Whether every employee has completed a training course
questions.explain: Regulators focus on the CDE concept from Lesson 16 — not universal perfection, but demonstrated control over the elements that actually matter for compliance.

questions.q: What does BCBS 239 explicitly require of banks, per this lesson?
options: The capability to identify and govern critical data elements used in risk reporting, with assigned ownership and documented lineage
That all customer data be stored exclusively in paper records
That banks never use SQL Server for any purpose
That every employee personally review every transaction
questions.explain: A bank that can't produce a CDE list with owners and lineage for its risk-reporting data is failing BCBS 239's requirement directly in a real audit.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe Sarbanes-Oxley's (SOX's) relationship to the CDE concept?
options: The data elements feeding a company's financial statements are functionally SOX's own version of a CDE list, even without using that exact term
SOX has no connection to data governance of any kind
SOX explicitly uses the term 'Critical Data Element' in its original legal text
SOX only applies to companies outside the United States
questions.explain: SOX requires documented, auditable controls over financial reporting — an auditor reviewing SOX controls is directly checking the same kind of documentation Chapter 4 teaches, even though SOX doesn't use the term 'CDE.'

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four things a regulatory audit typically checks, per this lesson?
options: Whether a documented CDE list actually exists
Whether every CDE has a named, accountable owner
Whether the organization's logo uses the correct shade of blue
Whether there's evidence validation rules and lineage are actually being run
questions.explain: The four real checks are: a documented list exists, every CDE has a named owner, evidence the rules are actually run, and a remediation history — branding details aren't part of a regulatory audit.

questions.q: Per this lesson, how does a regulatory audit's checklist relate to the CDE record fields taught in Lesson 18?
options: It maps directly onto them — Lesson 18's documentation requirements were direct preparation for exactly this kind of scrutiny
They are completely unrelated topics with no overlap
Lesson 18's fields were designed to intentionally fail any regulatory audit
Regulatory audits never look at documentation, only at raw data
questions.explain: The owner, validation rule, lineage, and escalation fields from Lesson 18 are exactly what a regulator looks for when checking a CDE program's maturity.
